sapience_notes.subject: A review draft and the text actually posted diverge, and the gap is where requests get lost
sapience_notes.value: The long draft (pr11-review.md) carried eight numbered requests; the condensed text the user posted carried three conditions and five follow-up bullets. Seven requests map cleanly. Request 8 (Point.history versus PointedModel.hist field name) appears nowhere in the posted review, in any form -- as do the typst status.typ stamp-commit nit, the lemmas-only control paragraph, and the instruction that PR #9 must drop its three renamed modules on rebase. Mapping a draft onto a posted review must be done by grepping the posted text for each item, not by assuming the condensation kept everything below the line; the assumption was wrong for one item in eight here.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh on a shared, concurrently-dispatched tree, measured
sapience_notes.value: Run unflagged for a four-file markdown edit, it derived 9 touched paths. Five belonged to concurrent sibling dispatches (specs/TODO.md, specs/state.json, specs/events.jsonl, and files under specs/980_* and specs/981_*), which pulled in the full 90-suite agent-system battery at roughly 6 minutes. Separately, neither specs/reviews/** file this task actually edited appeared in the derived set, because that directory is git-excluded at .git/info/exclude:20. So the narrowing over-selects siblings' work and under-selects git-excluded paths at the same time -- it is not a scoping guarantee in either direction.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic deploy-only tree's standing suite-failure baseline
sapience_notes.value: Nine agent-system suites fail here and are baseline, not regressions: there is no on-disk agent-system/ source store (fixtures report 'agent-system/extensions/core/... not found'), and the deployed .claude/ tree is stale for the core, lean and sapience extensions.
